note: Canonical target/countertarget pairs for the selectivity panel. This file is a
HUMAN POLICY INPUT, not a derived artifact: it is authored, hashed into the
panel manifest, and should be reviewed by someone with the relevant domain
knowledge before any selectivity claim is published.
It is deliberately a supplement, not the primary mechanism. Relatedness is
derived first from the exhaustive alignment table (identity >= 0.25 with
coverage >= 0.50), which needs no curation at all. This list adds pairs that
medicinal chemistry treats as selectivity questions even where sequence
identity is modest, and names them explicitly.
Failure mode is safe by construction: an accession that is wrong, obsolete or
absent from the corpus simply matches no construct, so it contributes no
pairs. A wrong entry cannot invent a selectivity pair, only miss one. The
panel report states how many listed pairs actually matched.
